SL-PDPA-S4: Develop and adopt a formal Data Protection Compliance Programme that addresses every obligation in Parts I–IV of the PDPA and assign responsibility for its maintenance to a designated person or team.
SL-PDPA-S5: Create a processing register that maps every personal data activity to a specific lawful basis under Schedule I (general data) or Schedule II (special categories), and review entries whenever a new processing activity is introduced.
SL-PDPA-S5-1: For each processing activity, record the exact Schedule I or Schedule II condition relied upon and keep this documentation available for regulatory inspection.
SL-PDPA-S5-2: Maintain a processing register entry per data category that states the applicable lawful basis, the purpose of processing, and the relevant Schedule reference, updated whenever processing conditions change.
SL-PDPA-S6: Define a clear, written purpose for every personal data collection activity before processing begins, and prohibit use of that data for any purpose incompatible with the stated one.
SL-PDPA-S6-1: Document the specific, explicit, and legitimate purpose for each processing activity in your Data Protection Management Programme and enforce purpose limitation through access controls and staff training.
SL-PDPA-S6-2: Where data is re-used for archiving, research, or statistical purposes, record why this falls within the section 6(2) exception and implement the safeguards required by section 10.
SL-PDPA-S7: Conduct a data minimisation review for each processing activity to confirm that only data which is adequate, relevant, and proportionate to the stated purpose is collected or retained.
SL-PDPA-S7-1: Audit existing data collection forms and intake processes to remove any fields that collect personal data beyond what is strictly necessary for the declared processing purpose.
SL-PDPA-S8: Establish a procedure for periodically verifying the accuracy of stored personal data and correcting or deleting inaccurate or outdated records without undue delay.
SL-PDPA-S8-1: Implement a scheduled accuracy review cycle (e.g. annual or event-triggered) for each personal data category and provide a mechanism for data subjects to request corrections.
SL-PDPA-S9: Define and document a maximum retention period for every category of personal data, and implement automated deletion or anonymisation once that period expires.
SL-PDPA-S9-1: Produce a data retention schedule listing each data category, its retention period, the justification for that period, and the deletion or anonymisation method to be applied at expiry.
SL-PDPA-S9-2: Configure your systems to automatically flag or delete personal data that has exceeded its documented retention period, and test this mechanism at least annually.
SL-PDPA-S9-3: Where consent is the lawful basis, ensure the consent record itself is retained only as long as needed to demonstrate lawfulness, and delete it according to the same retention schedule.
SL-PDPA-S10: Implement and document appropriate technical and organisational security measures — including encryption, access controls, and pseudonymisation — to prevent unauthorised access, loss, or destruction of personal data.
SL-PDPA-S10-1: Conduct a security risk assessment for each processing environment and apply the resulting controls (e.g. encryption at rest and in transit, role-based access, audit logging) before processing commences.
SL-PDPA-S11: Prepare a clear, concise, and easily accessible privacy notice for each data collection channel that covers all Schedule V items, and make it available in writing or electronically at the point of collection.
SL-PDPA-S11-1: Review all data collection touchpoints (forms, websites, contracts) to confirm that a compliant Schedule V privacy notice is presented to data subjects at or before the time of collection.
SL-PDPA-S11-2: Where personal data is obtained indirectly (not from the data subject), provide the required Schedule V information within one month of collection, or at the first communication with the data subject.
SL-PDPA-S12: Implement a Data Protection Management Programme that catalogues all processing activities, integrates into governance structures, includes an internal complaints mechanism, and is reviewed on a periodic basis.
SL-PDPA-S12-1: Build and maintain a DPMP that records evidence of compliance with sections 5–11, establishes internal oversight, and includes a breach identification mechanism linked to your incident response procedure.
SL-PDPA-S13: Establish a formal Subject Access Request procedure with a designated owner, a response template covering all Schedule V information, and a tracked workflow to respond within 21 working days.
SL-PDPA-S13-1: Publish a clear process for data subjects to submit access requests in writing, log every request received, and ensure responses include all information specified in Schedule V.
SL-PDPA-S14: Implement a documented consent withdrawal procedure that allows data subjects to opt out at any time without affecting the lawfulness of prior processing, and cease processing promptly upon withdrawal.
SL-PDPA-S14-1: Provide data subjects with a simple, accessible method (e.g. unsubscribe link, written request form) to withdraw consent, and process withdrawal requests within a defined SLA.
SL-PDPA-S14-2: Create a procedure for handling objection requests under Schedule I(e) or I(f), evaluate each objection on its merits, and cease further processing unless compelling legitimate grounds are demonstrated.
SL-PDPA-S15: Create a data breach response plan that includes a 72-hour notification window to the Authority, a template breach notification, and a log of all incidents and actions taken.
SL-PDPA-S15-1: Establish written procedures and designated contacts for identifying and escalating personal data breaches, including criteria distinguishing notifiable from non-notifiable incidents.
SL-PDPA-S15-2: Conduct a post-incident review after every notifiable breach to assess root cause, implement corrective controls, and update the breach notification procedure accordingly.
SL-PDPA-S16: Implement a rectification and erasure request procedure that responds within 21 working days, integrates with your processing systems to execute changes, and documents reasons for any refusal.
SL-PDPA-S16-1: Define the circumstances under which erasure requests must be fulfilled (e.g. unlawful processing, consent withdrawal, court order) and configure systems to execute deletion or restrict further processing accordingly.
SL-PDPA-S16-2: Where personal data must be retained for evidentiary or legal reasons, restrict further processing of that data while the retention obligation exists and document the basis for the restriction.
SL-PDPA-S17: Design a unified data subject rights workflow covering access, withdrawal, objection, rectification, and erasure requests, with a 21-working-day response target, a refusal policy, and an appeals notice.
SL-PDPA-S17-1: Train staff who handle data subject requests on the response timeline (21 working days), the permissible grounds for refusal under section 17(2), and the requirement to inform subjects of their right of appeal.
SL-PDPA-S17-2: Document the specific grounds (e.g. national security, criminal investigation, identity verification failure) under which a data subject request may be refused, and record each refusal decision with reasons.
SL-PDPA-S18: Identify all automated decision-making processes that could create irreversible or continuous impacts on data subjects, and implement a human review mechanism for affected decisions.
SL-PDPA-S18-1: Map every automated processing activity and determine whether it meets the threshold for section 18 (irreversible, continuous impact on rights); for those that do, build and publicise a request-for-review procedure.
SL-PDPA-S18-2: Where an automated decision-making exception under section 18(2) is relied upon, document the applicable exception (written law, consent, contract) and apply any Authority-specified safeguards.
SL-PDPA-S19: Establish an internal appeals-handling process for refused data subject requests and include the right to appeal to the Data Protection Authority in every refusal notice sent to data subjects.
SL-PDPA-S19-1: Include a clear statement of the right to appeal to the Authority, including the prescribed form and timeframe, in every notice of refusal issued under sections 14–18.
SL-PDPA-S19-2: Maintain records of all data subject refusals and the rationale for each, in a format that can be submitted to the Authority upon request during an appeal determination.
SL-PDPA-S20: Assess whether your organisation meets the mandatory DPO appointment criteria (public authority, systematic monitoring, or high-risk processing), appoint a qualified DPO where required, and publish their contact details.
SL-PDPA-S20-1: Carry out a DPO threshold assessment against the criteria in section 20(1), appoint a DPO with relevant data protection qualifications if the criteria are met, and communicate their details to the Authority.
SL-PDPA-S21: Review all third-party data processing relationships, confirm each processor is bound by a compliant data processing agreement covering subject-matter, duration, purpose, data type, and obligations.
SL-PDPA-S21-1: Audit every vendor or third-party service that processes personal data on your behalf; where no written data processing agreement exists, put one in place that meets the requirements of section 21(1)(b).
SL-PDPA-S22: Ensure all processors operate only under your written instructions, their staff are bound by confidentiality obligations, and they agree to return or destroy personal data at contract end.
SL-PDPA-S22-1: Update processor contracts to include written-instruction requirements, confidentiality obligations for personnel, audit facilitation rights, and a data return or destruction clause upon service termination.
SL-PDPA-S23: Develop and test a personal data breach notification procedure that meets the Authority's prescribed form, manner, and timeline requirements, including a process for notifying affected data subjects where required.
SL-PDPA-S23-1: Draft a breach notification template aligned with the Authority's prescribed format and establish an escalation path so that qualifying breaches are reported to the Authority within the required timeframe.
SL-PDPA-S24: Carry out a Data Protection Impact Assessment before commencing any processing that involves systematic profiling, monitoring of publicly accessible areas, or processing identified as high-risk by the Authority.
SL-PDPA-S24-1: Develop a DPIA template covering risk identification, the processing's impact on Part I obligations and Part II rights, proposed mitigation measures, and DPO input; complete it before any high-risk processing begins.
SL-PDPA-S25: Where a DPIA identifies a risk of harm to data subjects, implement risk mitigation measures before processing begins; if residual risks cannot be eliminated, consult the Authority prior to commencing processing.
SL-PDPA-S25-1: Document every risk of harm identified in a DPIA, assign a mitigation owner, and confirm all mitigations are in place before processing starts; retain evidence of these steps for Authority review.
SL-PDPA-S26: Establish a cross-border data transfer policy that identifies the legal mechanism for each transfer (adequacy decision or appropriate safeguards), and implement binding commitments with recipients in third countries.
SL-PDPA-S26-1: Identify all cross-border personal data flows and, for each, confirm whether the destination country has an adequacy decision; where none exists, apply Authority-specified safeguard instruments before transferring data.
SL-PDPA-S27: Obtain explicit consent before using any communication channel to send marketing or solicited messages, provide a free opt-out mechanism at every touchpoint, and disclose the sender identity and message nature in every communication.
SL-PDPA-S27-1: Implement a consent capture mechanism for all marketing communications that meets Schedule III conditions, and maintain a suppression list to prevent messages being sent to data subjects who have withdrawn consent or opted out.
